A small SaaS website doesn't need to compete for every popular keyword.

LowFruits helps find search terms with weaker competition.

These terms can be a better starting point for websites without the authority or resources to compete against established brands.

#SEO #BuildInPublic #IndieHacker

Your SaaS website doesn't always need a clickable link to get noticed.

When people discuss, recommend or reference your SaaS across the web, those mentions can contribute to your online visibility and reputation.

Don't overlook you SaaS brand awareness in your SEO strategy

#SEO #SaaS #IndieHacker

Does your SaaS have uniquie data from Users?

You could turn it into a collection of useful, searchable pages.

But don't just generate thousands of nearly identical pages. 

Start with 20 genuinely helpful ones and improve them based on what people need.

#SEO #SaaS #OrganicGrowth #IndieHacker

Good SaaS web content starts with understanding what users actually want to know.

AlsoAsked explores related questions potential users ask.

Discover questions worth answering, expand your blog topics and build more useful content for your SaaS audience.

People are increasingly asking AI to recommend SaaS's.

Try asking ChatGPT and Perplexity the questions your potential users ask.

Look at which websites appear in their answers. 

Study those sources and find legitimate opportunities to get backlinks from them.

#AISearch #SEO #SaaS #IndieHacker

Want people to follow your SaaS journey?

Show the actual work.

Share user feedback, traffic numbers, failed experiments and lessons learned.

You don't need to make every update look like a success story. 

Honest progress is often more interesting.

#BuildInPublic #IndieHackers #SaaS

One of the biggest mistakes in SEO is creating separate pages for keywords that belong together.

Keyword Insights groups related keywords into clusters, helping you decide which topics deserve individual pages.

A useful approach to planning a SaaS content strategy.

#SEO #SaaS #IndieHacker

Would you rather get one backlink from a site serving exactly your audience or ten links from unrelated high-authority sites?

A relevant link can bring the right visitors, and builds credibility for your SaaS website

Domain authority alone misses the point.

#SEO #LinkBuilding #SaaS #IndieHackers

Your potential users are already discussing their problems somewhere

Find the relevant subreddit, Slack group or Discord server

Spend time answering questions and helping people without immediately pitching your SaaS

Build trust before asking for attention.

#CommunityMarketing #SaaS #IndieHacker

As your SaaS blog grows, connecting related articles becomes increasingly important.

InLinks helps automate internal linking across your website.

Connect relevant guides, tutorials, feature pages and resources to make your SaaS blog easier to navigate.

#TechnicalSEO #ContentMarketing #IndieHacker

Reddit discussions, niche forums and online communities can be valuable sources of referral traffic and SaaS discovery.

The key is participation. Answer questions, share useful resources and become part of the conversation.

Don't link spam these places.

#SEO #OrganicGrowth #SaaS #IndieHacker

Sometimes you need the right partner.

Find another founder serving the same audience with a complementary SaaS product

Exchange newsletter mentions, create a joint resource or host a webinar together

Both SaaS products get exposure to the audience

#SaaS #Partnerships #OrganicGrowth #IndieHacker

What if your next SaaS blog post started with actual search data instead of a random content idea?

Obbio AI helps turn Google Search Console opportunities into blog posts and landing pages.

A different approach to deciding what your SaaS blog should publish next.

Some SaaS blog owners avoid linking to other websites because they fear losing visitors or authority

But linking to useful, relevant sources helps readers explore a topic more deeply.

Good content doesn't have to pretend that other useful websites don't exist.

#SEO #ContentMarketing #IndieHacker

Your SaaS tool can be discovered through AI answers, not just traditional Google search results.

OtterlyAI tracks brand and competitor mentions and citations across AI-generated answers.

It's useful for monitoring how your SaaS appears in the AI search landscape.

#AISearch #SEO #SaaS #IndieHacker

200 backlinks in one month and none for the next months isn't  a great growth strategy for your SaaS blog.

Focus on consistently earning genuine recommendations, useful references and relevant mentions.

Sustainable SEO is about building credibility over time.

#SEO #LinkBuilding #IndieHacker

SaaS websites growing sustainably aren't necessarily the ones with the biggest backlink counts

They're the ones earning attention from relevant publications, communities, customers and industry peers.

Stop treating backlinks like a numbers game
